name: IT Operations Team
description: An IT/Operations department template for companies of any size (3-20 FTE). This template covers an operations team with an IT Manager, System Administrator, Network Engineer, Help Desk Lead, Help Desk Agents, Security Administrator, and a General Purpose Operator (GPO). It provides comprehensive IT infrastructure management including infrastructure administration, network management, security operations, help desk support, user provisioning, and disaster recovery. Designed for organizations that need reliable, secure, and scalable IT operations with clear service level expectations.

metadata.industry: All industries -- Finance, Healthcare, Education, Government, Technology

agents.name: IT Manager
agents.description: IT department leader responsible for strategic planning, budget management, vendor relationships, policy governance, service level management, and cross-functional coordination with business units.

agents.name: System Administrator
agents.description: Infrastructure specialist responsible for server administration, operating system management, virtualization, cloud infrastructure, system monitoring, and backup/recovery operations.

agents.name: Network Engineer
agents.description: Network infrastructure specialist responsible for network design, configuration, troubleshooting, firewall management, VPN administration, and network performance optimization.

agents.name: Help Desk Lead
agents.description: Help desk team leader responsible for ticket management, SLA enforcement, team coordination, escalation handling, knowledge base maintenance, and service desk operations.

agents.name: Help Desk Agent
agents.description: First-line IT support agent responsible for handling user tickets, basic troubleshooting, password resets, software installation, and escalation of complex issues to senior team members.

agents.name: Security Administrator
agents.description: Security specialist responsible for security monitoring, vulnerability management, access control, incident response, compliance audits, and security policy enforcement.

agents.name: Operations GPO
agents.description: Operational support agent handling IT asset management, documentation, reporting, automated provisioning, compliance tracking, and administrative tasks.

workflows.name: Incident Management Workflow
workflows.description: ITIL-aligned incident management process for detecting, classifying, resolving, and documenting IT incidents with appropriate escalation paths.

steps.description: Detect incident through monitoring alerts or user ticket. Log incident in the ITSM system with initial classification, priority level, and affected services
Classify incident severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low) based on business impact and urgency. Assign to the appropriate support tier
Diagnose root cause using monitoring tools, logs, and diagnostic procedures. Implement resolution or workaround. If unresolved, escalate to the appropriate specialist
Send status updates to affected users and stakeholders at defined intervals. Critical incidents trigger executive notification
Verify with the user that the issue is fully resolved and services are operating normally. Document resolution details in the incident record
Close the incident, update knowledge base with resolution steps, and identify if post-incident review or preventive action is required

workflows.name: Change Management Workflow
workflows.description: ITIL-aligned change management process for evaluating, approving, implementing, and reviewing changes to the IT infrastructure with minimal disruption.

steps.description: Submit change request with description, rationale, implementation plan, rollback plan, risk assessment, and estimated impact window
Categorize the change: Standard (pre-approved), Normal (requires CAB review), or Emergency (security hotfix, critical outage fix)

For Normal changes, CAB (Change Advisory Board) reviews impact, risk, and implementation plan. For Standard changes, verify against approved templates. For Emergency changes, provide rapid approval with post-hoc review
Implement the change during the approved maintenance window following the documented implementation plan. Execute rollback procedures if issues arise
Verify the change was successful: services running correctly, no regressions, performance within normal parameters
Document the change in the change log, capture lessons learned, update documentation, and close the change request in the ITSM system

workflows.name: User Provisioning Workflow
workflows.description: Automated user provisioning and deprovisioning process covering account creation, access assignment, resource allocation, and timely offboarding.

steps.description: Receive user provisioning request from HR system or manager. Validate the request with the appropriate approver based on access level and policy
Determine the user's access profile based on role, department, and least-privilege principles. Assign to appropriate groups and define resource access
Create accounts in Active Directory, email system, SaaS applications, and other managed systems. Set initial passwords and enforce MFA
Allocate hardware (laptop, peripherals), software licenses, cloud resources, and access to shared drives or collaboration tools
Notify the user and their manager that accounts are ready. Send onboarding checklist and provide access credentials securely
Log the provisioning action for audit compliance. Add user to the access review schedule for periodic credential review

workflows.name: Backup and Recovery Workflow
workflows.description: Systematic backup operations and disaster recovery procedures ensuring data integrity, availability, and tested recovery capabilities.

steps.description: Execute scheduled backups according to the backup policy: full backups (weekly), incremental backups (daily), and transaction log backups (hourly for critical databases)
Verify backup integrity through checksums, size validation, and automated restore tests. Alert on any backup failures or anomalies
Execute periodic disaster recovery tests (quarterly minimum): restore from backup to isolated environment and verify data integrity and application functionality
Document backup and recovery test results including RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective) achievement. Identify any gaps
Adjust backup schedules, retention policies, and storage allocation based on test results, changing data volumes, and business requirements
Generate backup compliance reports for audit purposes. Document backup coverage across all critical systems and regulatory requirements

workflows.name: Capacity Planning Workflow
workflows.description: Proactive capacity planning process for monitoring resource utilization, forecasting growth, and preventing infrastructure bottlenecks.

steps.description: Gather current utilization data across all infrastructure: CPU, memory, storage, network bandwidth, license counts, and user counts
Analyze utilization trends over the past 6-12 months. Identify systems approaching capacity thresholds and trending toward saturation
Project future demand based on business growth plans, new initiatives, and seasonal patterns. Identify capacity gaps and timeline for action
Recommend infrastructure actions: hardware procurement, cloud scaling, license purchases, optimization projects, or architecture changes
Present capacity plan to leadership for budget approval. Prioritize actions based on risk, cost, and business impact
Track capacity improvement actions to completion. Update monitoring dashboards and verify that capacity thresholds are met after implementation

episodic_memory.description: Records incident histories, change records, user provisioning events, backup test results, and compliance audit findings

procedural_memory.description: Caches operational procedures, deployment scripts, troubleshooting sequences, backup procedures, and disaster recovery runbooks

governance_rules.name: Change Management Requirement
governance_rules.rule: All changes to production infrastructure must follow the change management process. No emergency changes without post-hoc CAB review within 48 hours. Standard changes must use approved templates and runbooks.

governance_rules.name: Access Control and Least Privilege
governance_rules.rule: All user and service accounts must follow the principle of least privilege. Access must be reviewed quarterly. Administrative access requires multi-factor authentication. Unexplained access requests must be escalated to the Security Administrator.

governance_rules.name: Backup and Recovery Compliance
governance_rules.rule: All critical systems must have documented backup procedures with verified restore capability. Backup tests must be performed quarterly. RPO must not exceed 24 hours for critical systems and 72 hours for non-critical systems.

governance_rules.name: Security Patch Management
governance_rules.rule: Critical security patches must be applied within 7 days of release. High-severity patches within 30 days. All patching must be tested in a non-production environment first. Emergency patches for active exploits must be applied immediately with documented justification.

governance_rules.name: Incident Response and Escalation
governance_rules.rule: All incidents must be logged in the ITSM system with proper classification and priority. P1 incidents must be acknowledged within 30 minutes and escalated to the IT Manager within 60 minutes. Post-incident review required for all P1 incidents within 5 business days.

governance_rules.name: Compliance and Audit Readiness
governance_rules.rule: All IT operations must maintain compliance with relevant regulations (GDPR, HIPAA, SOX, PCI-DSS as applicable). Quarterly compliance audits required. Documentation must be current and accessible to auditors.

kpis.name: System Uptime
kpis.description: Percentage of time critical IT systems and services are available and operational

kpis.name: Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR)
kpis.description: Average time from incident detection to full resolution
kpis.target: under 4 hours for P1, under 8 hours for P2

kpis.name: Ticket Resolution Time
kpis.description: Average time to resolve user support tickets by priority level
kpis.target: P1: 1 hour, P2: 4 hours, P3: 1 business day, P4: 3 business days

kpis.name: Security Incidents
kpis.description: Number of security incidents (breaches, policy violations, vulnerabilities) per quarter

kpis.name: User Satisfaction Score
kpis.description: Average user satisfaction rating from post-incident and support ticket surveys

kpis.name: Backup Success Rate
kpis.description: Percentage of scheduled backups that complete successfully without errors

kpis.name: First Call Resolution Rate
kpis.description: Percentage of user tickets resolved on first contact without requiring follow-up or escalation

kpis.name: Patch Compliance Rate
kpis.description: Percentage of systems with security patches applied within the required timeframe

operational_policies.name: Help Desk Support Hours and Escalation
operational_policies.description: Standard support hours are Monday-Friday 8:00-18:00. Extended hours and weekend support for critical systems as defined in the SLA. P1 incidents require 24/7 coverage with the Security Administrator or System Administrator on call. Escalation path: Help Desk Agent -> Help Desk Lead -> System Administrator/Network Engineer -> IT Manager. Response SLAs: P1 (30 min), P2 (2 hours), P3 (1 business day), P4 (3 business days).

operational_policies.name: Change Management and Maintenance Windows
operational_policies.description: All production infrastructure changes must follow the change management process with documented approval. Standard maintenance windows are Saturday 02:00-06:00 and Sunday 00:00-04:00 (local time). Emergency changes require rapid CAB review within 48 hours. All changes must have a documented rollback plan.

operational_policies.name: Security and Access Control Policy
operational_policies.description: All systems require MFA for administrative access. User access reviews conducted quarterly. Password policy: minimum 12 characters, complexity requirements, 90-day rotation for privileged accounts. Security awareness training required annually for all staff. Incident response plan reviewed and tested biannually.
